narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 41% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reason the model is concerned is that you’ve said you don’t plan to continue your education after high school. Almost all students who aren’t required to take remedial courses say they want to go on to university or college, so this difference stands out. The model sees this as a strong signal that you might struggle to finish the year successfully.

On a more positive note, you’ve never failed a class before, which works in your favor. This shows you have a solid academic foundation, and the model takes that into account. Additionally, your guardian being your father rather than your mother slightly reduces the risk in the model’s eyes, though this factor is less important than the others.

To improve your chances, focus on setting clear goals for your future—whether that’s further education, training, or a career path. Even if you’re unsure about university, having a plan can help you stay motivated. The remedial courses will give you extra time and support to strengthen your skills, so take full advantage of them. Small steps, like increasing your weekly study time or finding ways to balance your free time, can also make a big difference. You’ve got the ability to succeed, and these courses are here to help you do just that.
